Bachelor Party Transportation Scottsdale: Rates & Seats

Scottsdale Sprinters runs bachelor party transportation in Scottsdale as a chauffeured vehicle booked by the hour, against a published rate, minimum and seat count. Party units carry the occasion, from the 13-seat Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) at $175 an hour to the 28-seat Party Bus (28 Pax) at $250 an hour and the 18-seat Pink Hummer Limo at $295 an hour. Each carries a 4-hour minimum, so a booking starts between $700 and $1,180 before 8% tax. Below: every unit by seat and per-seat cost, how a golf day and a night out fit inside one 7-hour booking, and what the house rules allow. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

What does Scottsdale Sprinters run for a bachelor party?

Scottsdale Sprinters runs party units for a bachelor party in Scottsdale, led by the 18-seat Pink Hummer Limo and the 28-seat Party Bus (28 Pax). What does bachelor party transportation cost in Scottsdale?

Scottsdale Sprinters prices a bachelor party by the hour against a published minimum, so the 28-seat Party Bus (28 Pax) starts at $1,000 — $250 an hour across its 4-hour minimum, before 8% tax. Across a full bus that is about $36 a seat. The same arithmetic runs on every unit. The Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) and the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) share $175, so both open at $700; the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter opens at $1,000 and the Pink Hummer Limo at $1,180. Those are the current published hourly rates and minimums. Hours past the minimum bill at the same rate. The worked example this page already publishes runs 7 hours on the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax), of which 1 is free, so it bills as 6 — $1,050, about $66 a head across 16 seats.

Can one booking cover a golf day and a night out?

Yes, and it is one reservation rather than two. A bachelor booking is hours with a chauffeur, not a route we sell you: the example this page publishes is 7 hours, the clock runs from first pickup to last drop-off, and stops inside it cost nothing. That is what makes a morning tee time and an evening in Old Town Scottsdale one booking: the vehicle waits through the round, the shower stop and dinner, and nobody has to be the designated driver. Course access and where a commercial vehicle may stop are the property's call. The window is the product: "Hourly charters start at four hours. The vehicle stays with your group for the whole booked window, so the clock runs from pickup to the last drop-off, not per stop. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged." The pickup instruction this page publishes: "One pickup address for the whole group and one phone we call — the best man, not the group chat. Put every stop on the reservation before the night starts; stops on an hourly charter cost nothing, so list them all." The bags, as the page already states them: "Golf bags, coolers and overnight bags all compete for the same floor. Say what is coming when you request the quote and we confirm the fit in writing rather than at the curb." Beyond that: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

What are the drinking rules on a bachelor party vehicle?

The 2 rules that decide this are house rules, quoted below word for word rather than summarised. They apply on every trip Scottsdale Sprinters runs, whatever the vehicle and whatever the occasion, and no bachelor booking waives them or adds to them. The rules as published: "Passengers 21 and over bring their own alcohol, and we do not sell it. Arizona vehicle-for-hire open-container policy, A.R.S. § 4-251, allows it, and if anyone under 21 rides, no alcohol comes on that trip." and "No underage drinking. Anyone under 21 stays on soft drinks." Those 2 sentences are the site's whole age policy. Beyond them this page states nothing. Scottsdale Sprinters publishes no bar package, no supplied alcohol and no drinks minimum, so none is claimed here. A group with guests under 21 should say so when requesting the quote and have it confirmed in writing. Two more decide how the night ends: "Keep the drinks in the cups. Minor spills are fine; a can or two on the floor counts as excessive and carries a cleaning fee." ($450). "If someone gets sick in the vehicle, we have to deep clean it, and that carries a cleaning fee. Pace yourselves." ($450). And one that is not about money: "Be kind to your chauffeur. They are the reason everyone gets home."

What is included on board, and what is not?

One page of house rules governs every trip here, and 3 of those rules carry a stated fee. Drinking is allowed for guests 21 and over, eating is not, and smoking or vaping carries a $1,500 fee no bachelor booking waives. What comes with the vehicle: "Bottled water is on board and it is the only complimentary amenity; everything else is an add-on you choose at checkout." Eating is a separate rule: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." "No smoking or vaping of any kind. The smell does not leave, so this one carries a fee." ($1,500). Stops cost nothing on an hourly charter; the $50 stop fee belongs to a point-to-point transfer instead. Condition is documented, not argued afterwards. "Before every trip your chauffeur takes a documented set of photos of the interior. They are for our internal records only." "You authorize us to charge the card on file for damage beyond normal use. We will never charge for damage without telling you first, with the photos, so there are no surprises."
